title: Every interface names one specific command
statement: The CLI (`lathe <aggregate> <command>`), the MCP tools (`<aggregate>_<command>`, one per command) and HTTP (`POST /api/<aggregate>/<command>`) MUST each name the one command they run, taking the command's own fields, each checked against its column in the schema; none MAY take a table or kind name and dispatch by it.

title: A refusal gives every reason and changes nothing
statement: When a command is refused, the CLI MUST print every reason with the rule it broke and exit with an error, an MCP tool MUST return the refusal with its reasons and HTTP MUST answer 422 with them; no data file MAY change.

title: A write is all or nothing
statement: A write's commands MUST all take effect or none: when one is refused, the data and every data file stay as they were.

title: A write is checked whole before any file changes
statement: Each write MUST build the new state in one transaction, with every key, constraint and validation query of the schema, and MUST rewrite a data file only after the whole state passes.

title: A write rewrites only its tables' files, in one fixed form
statement: A write MUST rewrite only the data files of the tables it changed, each through a temporary file and a rename, rows sorted by key and columns in the table's order, so the same data always gives the same file and a changed row is a one-line diff.

title: Writes run one after another
statement: Writes to one store MUST run one at a time, each on the state the one before it left, so two writers never lose each other's change.

title: A refusal names every problem and where it is
statement: A refused write or load MUST name every problem it found, each with its rule, a message naming the table, row and value, and the data file and line of a loaded row or the index of the command that brought it.

title: A record has every column its kind requires
statement: A record MUST have a value of the right type for each required column of its kind's table, and no column its table lacks.

title: A test starts from its aggregate's own data set
statement: A test MUST start only from test data sets of its own aggregate, each built with that aggregate's own Add commands, never from a shared fixture of every kind.

title: Layout lives in the markup
statement: A component MUST render its own structure: the rows, columns and slots its parts sit in. A stylesheet MUST NOT move an element into another element's box or restyle it from outside its component, so no `display: contents` and no `:has()`. When a control from further down belongs in a heading's row, the heading offers a slot and the control renders into it, as a section's header row holds its list's Expand all.
notes: Absolute positioning stays for marks and decorations inside a component's own box, such as a graph node's chevron.

title: Styles are set by class
statement: A style rule MUST select by class, attribute or ID. A selector that names only elements, such as `header`, MUST NOT be used outside the base styles, because it reaches every such element on every page, including ones added later. The base styles may set the page and its plain text and controls: `html`, `body`, headings, paragraphs, links, code, and form controls.

title: Colors and shadows are tokens
statement: A color, including a shadow's color and the backdrop behind drawers and dialogs, MUST be a custom property defined in `:root` (with its dark value in the dark theme), and every rule MUST use it through `var()`. Component inline styles MUST NOT set colors. A size several rules share, such as `--node-radius`, SHOULD be a token too.

title: Generic components know nothing of specs
statement: A component in `app/src/components` MUST import only React and other generic components, never the spec pages, the graph, the shell or the data types. What a spec page needs from it comes in through props, such as a list's items, its row renderer and its label. A page of a spec kind is never a generic component: each aggregate owns its page and its editor, in its own slice (`app/src/<domain>/<aggregate>/`), found by the Record page in its typed list.

title: Kind labels become plural only through plural() and lowercase only through lowerLabel()
statement: Code MUST make a kind's label plural with `plural()` from `app/src/plural.ts`, never by adding an "s", so every page and the graph say "Capabilities" and "Open questions" the same way. Inside a sentence a label MUST be lowercased with `lowerLabel()`, which keeps an acronym such as "UC requirement" whole, never with `toLowerCase()`.

title: Every control has an accessible name
statement: Every button, link and form control MUST have an accessible name: its text, an `aria-label`, or a label. An icon-only button names what it does ("Collapse LA-TRC-UC09"), and a control with a keyboard shortcut also states it in `aria-keyshortcuts`.

title: American spelling
statement: Code, UI text, specs and docs MUST use American spelling, such as modeling, color, center, behavior, organize and labeled. Fixed external names keep theirs, such as the HTML attribute `aria-labelledby`.

title: Every grid says its columns
statement: A CSS grid that lays out items in columns MUST declare `grid-template-columns`, and a single column MUST be `minmax(0, 1fr)`. A grid with no column template sizes its column to its widest content, so a long title or a wide list would widen the column past its panel and be cut off, instead of shrinking, wrapping or truncating. A grid that only centers one item (`place-items`) lays out no columns.

title: Themes only set tokens
statement: Every visual value (color, font, text size, density, radius, gap and motion speed) MUST come from a token in `:root`, so that a theme can change it. A theme MUST be data that sets those tokens and nothing else: its file names token names only, and the stylesheet written from it MUST have no selector but `:root` and set only custom properties. Every built-in theme MUST pass WCAG AA in both its light and dark sets: body text, muted text and the accent at least 4.5:1 on the page and on a sheet.

title: One address per thing
statement: A record's address MUST be its bare ID (`/LA-TRC-UC09`), a product's and a domain's included, and a group's MUST be its place in the graph's tree: a stage or folder under its domain (`/LA-EXP/define/use-cases`), or a record's group of one kind of child (`/<parent-id>/<kind>`). The app's one page of its own is the products picker at `/`; every tool opens over the stage in the query of the focus it is over (`?panel=checks`, `?page=format/kinds/<kind>`, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R20`), so no address of the app can clash with an ID, which starts with a capital. Every address of a record or group MUST be built by `addressOf` in `app/src/views/address.ts`, the one function that makes them: no other file MAY build such a path by hand. An address that changes form changes everywhere at once, with no redirect from the old one (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R20`).

title: Changes are hard cutovers
statement: When something is renamed or reshaped (an address, a function's signature, a command ID, a stored key, a class, a column or a label), every call site, record and test MUST move to the new form in the same change, and the old form MUST be deleted. The code MUST NOT keep redirects, aliases, second signatures, upgrades of saved state, or old names kept to avoid churn. Saved state in an old form is dropped: a stored entry that is not valid today is ignored, never converted.

title: Nothing outlives its purpose
statement: When a behavior is removed or replaced, everything that only served it MUST go in the same change: its code, exports, files and dependencies, its styles, its commands and icons, its tests and its records. The code MUST NOT keep a file, export or dependency nothing uses, a class selector nothing draws, a command nothing handles or nothing can reach, or an icon nothing shows. Every mark the Graph or the ERD stage can draw (a box's shape or fill, a badge, a line style) MUST be listed in that stage's key with what it means: a mark that can't be explained can't ship. Each of these is checked, so a leftover fails instead of surviving because nobody remembered it.

title: Everything clickable shows a hover state
statement: Anything the pointer can click (a card, a graph node, a row in a menu, a button) MUST change when the pointer is over it, and only clickable things MAY. Every hover uses the shared tokens in `:root`: `--hover-bg` tints rows and plain buttons, `--hover-ring` rings cards and graph nodes, and `--hover-speed` times the change, which reduced motion turns off. A card takes the ring anywhere on it, from its title stretched over it (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`). A graph node that is not clickable, such as the center or a file, keeps the default cursor and no hover.

title: The stage behind, panels floating over it, every panel edge resizes
statement: On a wide screen a focus page MUST read as one stage filling the window behind everything, with every other part floating over it as an inset, frosted panel: the navigation, the tab panel (the page bar and the header strip), and the wiki card, each a rounded box a gap (`--float-inset`) from the window and from each other, with a soft shadow. Frosted means a mostly opaque surface (`--float-dense`, about 82%, for the nav, the tab panel and the chat, `--float-light`, about 72%, for the wiki card) over a strong backdrop blur (`--float-blur`, 22 px), the stage showing through as shape and color while text keeps WCAG 2.2 AA contrast; the surfaces are tokens with light and dark values, and under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` every panel MUST be opaque. A page without a stage floats as one panel right of the nav. The inner edge of each resizable panel MUST be a `ResizeHandle` from `app/src/components/ResizeHandle.tsx`, the one component that draws a splitter, so each handle drags, steps with the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps), jumps with Home and End, resets on double-click and is remembered alike. On a narrow screen the nav is a drawer, the wiki card a bottom sheet, and nothing is resizable.

title: The page's controls sit apart from a stage's tools, which float in the open space
statement: The page's controls and the stage's own controls MUST sit apart. In the desktop app the page bar, floating across the top of the stage right of the nav, MUST hold the space's tabs at its left and, at its right, the stage switch (a group labeled "Stage" whose buttons carry `aria-pressed`) and then the wiki card toggle; it MUST keep one fixed height (`--page-bar-height`) on one line whatever it holds, its tabs scrolling sideways, so nothing below it moves. On the web, wide, where the browser's tabs are the tabs, there MUST be no page bar: the stage switch and the wiki card toggle MUST sit at the right of the header strip's row, so no row stands empty. Every stage's toolbar (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R21`), with its shared controls and the stage's own, MUST float inside the open space the panels leave, marked `data-stage-tools="top"`, never with the page's controls and never as a header of its own above the stage. A toggle that is on, a pressed stage or a shown panel, MUST use the one shared on look (`icon-button is-on`), and stage switches and layout actions MUST NOT appear anywhere else on the page.
notes:
In the desktop app the page bar is the top of the tab panel (`page-bar`), the tabs (`role="tablist"`) at its left and its actions (`page-bar-actions`) at its right, a thin divider before the wiki card toggle; the header strip (`LA-V96-R09`) sits directly under it. The stage's own controls are the graph's layout, depth and filters, and the trace's Gaps only filter.

On a phone the page bar is the same bar, compact (`page-bar is-compact`), under the shell's top bar: in the desktop app an "Open pages" button that opens the tabs as a sheet takes the tabs' place, the stage switch shows the three stages, and the wiki card toggle stays at the far right.

title: Motion is shared and optional
statement: Every transition and animation MUST take its time and easing from the shared tokens in `:root`: `--motion-speed` and `--motion-ease` for things that move or fade, and `--hover-speed` for hover. Each one MUST be turned off when the system asks for reduced motion, by a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule for the same selector or by applying only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`. Animation in JS MUST read the same tokens and check `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`, jumping straight to the end when it matches; `readMotion()` in `app/src/graph/motion.ts` does both. Motion only helps the eye follow a change: nothing may depend on it.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link
statement: A list row that leads to one record MUST be clickable anywhere on it, through one real link (`<a href>`) to that record, marked `row-link`, whose `::after` stretches over the whole row (`position: absolute; inset: 0`, the row being `position: relative`), as a card's title does (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`). A plain click navigates within the app; Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click open a new tab, because it is a real link. A row MUST have exactly one such link, and every other control in it (a fold chevron, another record link such as "followed by UC01", a badge with a tooltip, a button) MUST sit above the stretched link through one shared rule, so a click on it does what it would without the link.
notes: The row takes the link's hover (the `--hover-bg` tint, the title in steel) and its focus ring, while keyboard focus stays on the one link. A row's plain text cannot be drag-selected; that is accepted. A list that does not navigate, such as the wiki card's summary facts, is not a row of this kind.

title: Every open thing has an address
statement: Anything a person can open MUST be reachable from the address bar or restorable from storage, so a reload brings it back as it was: a page and its stage are in the address (`/<id>?stage=erd`), and what the address cannot hold, such as the desktop app's open tabs, which one is active and each tab's place and history, a browser tab's depth, filters and wiki card, and the session's settings, is kept in session or local storage and read back on load. A new kind of open thing (a tab, a stage, a panel state worth sharing) MUST come with a test that opens it, reloads the app at the same address and expects the same thing open. Storage is read with guards (`readPref`), so a missing or malformed value falls back to a default and never breaks the page.

title: Everything works by touch
statement: The app MUST work with a finger as well as a mouse. On a coarse pointer (`@media (pointer: coarse)`), every control's target MUST be at least 44 × 44 px (`--touch-target`): the control itself, or for a control drawn small inside a row or a node (a fold chevron, a tab's close button), a `::before` stretched around it, so its look does not change. No action or information MAY be reachable only by hover: a control a hover reveals MUST show always on a coarse pointer, and where a click opens something at once, a tap MUST first say what it is (`LA-V93-R02`). No page MAY scroll sideways at 320 px wide.
notes:
Canvas nodes, laid out by the canvas and zoomed by a pinch, and whole cards are targets of their own size. A tooltip only repeats a name and keys the control already has, and opens on keyboard focus too. To keep pages from scrolling sideways, no rule fixes a least width wider than the phone's content (288 px) outside a wide-screen media query; long IDs wrap; wide tables and code blocks scroll in their own box.

Proved in `app/test/standards.test.tsx` by reading the stylesheet and rendering the main pages on a phone; what jsdom cannot lay out is checked in a browser at 320 and 375 px.

title: Nothing jumps
statement: Nothing on screen MAY move unless the Reader moved it or it moves by a deliberate motion on the shared tokens (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`). In every scenario of the stability suite (`app/stability`, run by `npm --prefix app run test:stability`), the layout shifts that the step does not mean to make MUST add up to 0.01 or less, counting the shifts just after input that CLS leaves out, and the key elements of the page (the nav, the tab panel, the header strip, the wiki card, the stage's canvas) MUST keep their boxes: they never move, jump back, or get thrown away and drawn anew. The causes that show in the source are checked without a browser too: every scroll box sets `scrollbar-gutter: stable`; a bar over the stage has a fixed block size or is one line cut with an ellipsis; a count or caption that changes is one text; a canvas stays mounted while its content changes and is fitted before its first paint; and what one part tells another (a stage telling the header strip its counts) arrives before paint. The causes and their fixes are listed in `notes/jitter-audit.md`.

title: Actions look like actions
statement: A standalone action MUST be the app's one `Button` component (`app/src/components/Button.tsx`), never a link dressed as text and never a button with a style of its own, in one of its three variants: ghost, the default; primary, for the one main action of a form or dialog; or icon, which MUST be given an accessible name. An action that goes to an address MUST be a real link drawn as a button (`buttonClass()` on a router link, or `Button` with `href`), so Cmd/Ctrl-click still opens a new tab.
notes:
- **Ghost**: no border or fill, padded, the `--hover-bg` tint on hover, the shared focus ring and an optional leading icon. "Expand all", "Clear filters", "Open the product overview", Cancel, Export and the desktop app's file actions are ghost buttons.
- **Primary**: filled with the accent, such as Save.
- **Icon**: a square ghost button that holds only an icon, such as the wiki card's collapse button or the nav's toggle.

On a coarse pointer a button is a 44 px target (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`).

Links stay links where they are navigation in context: inside prose (Markdown, or a sentence such as "See all products"), inside lists and rows (record references and the row links of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`), in breadcrumbs, and in the navigation. Controls that are not standalone actions keep their own form: tabs, toggles in a group (the stage switch, the graph's depth), fold chevrons, the nav's rows and a card's title, stretched over its card (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`).

Proved in `app/test/standards.test.tsx` by rendering the main pages and reading the source.

title: Every page passes the accessibility audit
statement: Every page and state the app draws MUST pass the accessibility suite (`app/a11y`, run by `npm --prefix app run test:a11y`), with no finding: 0 WCAG 2.2 AA violations on every page and state the suite visits.
notes:
- **The audit:** axe-core at WCAG 2.2 AA on the product, domain, record and group pages, each stage with the panels open and collapsed, Checks, Format and Appearance, quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, a tooltip and the phone's drawers and sheets, at 1440 px and 375 px, in the Lathe theme and High contrast, each in light and dark, and under reduced transparency.
- **What axe can't see**, walked by keyboard: Tab reaches every control and comes back round with no trap; the main tasks (open a record, switch stages, collapse the wiki card, re-center the graph, fold rows, pick a theme) work by keyboard alone; focus stays on the page after a move and returns to the opener when a dialog or a sheet closes; the announcer says what changed.

A finding is fixed by its cause, across the app, and the cause and fix are listed in `notes/a11y-audit.md`. The suite runs on the stability suite's harness (Playwright with Chromium, one worker, a free port), and is run with it for every UI change.

title: Lathe stays within its performance budgets
statement: The app MUST stay within its performance budgets, measured on the production build in Chromium on the dev machine by the performance suite (`app/perf`, run by `npm --prefix app run test:perf` after the stability suite for a UI change), whose budgets are in `app/perf/budgets.ts`, among them a record page interactive within 1.5 s and a stage switch within 100 ms of main-thread work.

title: Every drawn box shows its name
statement: In every layout of the graph (Tree and Nested, and any layout added later), at every focus and depth, every box the app draws MUST show its name: its title in full, wrapped on whole words and never clipped, and its kind and ID line, at the box's fixed size in the map, until its title would be drawn under 5 pixels on screen, where no text can be read and the box is drawn as a plain block, its fill and edge alone. A box is either drawn with its label, drawn as a block, or not drawn at all: off screen, under about 3 pixels, or past the drawing budget, a bar or its parent stands for it (`LA-EXP-DS10`). In every layout siblings are the same size with one text scale, the largest at which every sibling's whole label fits its box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), so every label fits its box by construction; a very small box has very small text, read by zooming in, and below the readable size it is a block.
notes: It is proved at the unit level by a sweep over the repo's own specs (Lathe's and the Tool Library's), every layout, every domain, stage and folder focused at depths 1 to 3 in a 770 by 640 and a 1200 by 800 frame with the real camera (`app/test/graph/readable.test.ts`, in `npm --prefix app test`), and in the browser by the stability suite, which focuses each of Lathe's domains in each layout and checks every drawn box has visible title text.

title: Labels read in sentence case
statement: Every label, heading, button and field name the app shows MUST read in sentence case: only its first word, and any name of a thing, starts with a capital. No style MAY change a label's letter case word by word (CSS text-transform: capitalize); a label that wants a capital first letter MUST get it from its own text or ::first-letter.

title: A card has one primary action, taken by clicking anywhere on it
statement: Every card MUST have one primary action, opening what the card is or using it, whichever fits, and a click or tap anywhere on the card MUST take it: no card is a dead box. A card MUST be the app's one `Card` component (`app/src/shell/Card.tsx`), which requires its primary action, an address (`href`) or an action (`onActivate`), so a card without one does not compile. The card's title is that real link or button, and the title's `::after` stretches over the whole card (`position: absolute`, the card being `position: relative`), so the card has one tab stop and one accessible name, and Enter or Space takes its action.
notes:
Any other link or button in the card (a record named in its text, a theme's Duplicate and edit, Edit and Export, the tap card's let go) sits above the stretched title, through one shared rule, and does what it says. The whole card takes the title's hover ring (`--hover-ring`), its focus ring and the pointer. No element outside the component uses the card classes (`card`, `card-*`), and no stylesheet styles a card class the component does not set.

The cards and their primary actions:
- **Products page:** each product's card opens its product page.
- **Product page:** each business outcome's card opens the outcome; each domain's card opens the domain page.
- **Appearance:** each theme's card uses the theme, and shows it as the one in use.
- **Trace view:** each card in an obligation's chain opens its record (a file's, the record that names it); the obligation's own card is marked as the current page.
- **Graph and ERD views by touch:** the card of a tapped node opens the node.

A problem row is a row of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`, not a card, but it is never a dead box either: it opens its record, or its check's page when it names no record or the page is the record's own.

title: A stage with one folder shows its records directly
statement: A stage with only one folder MUST show that folder's records directly under the stage, with no folder level between: a domain's Use cases, which holds only capabilities, reads Use cases › Record authoring, not Use cases › Capabilities › Record authoring. A stage with two or more folders MUST keep them. It holds for every stage of every product, Shared included, decided per domain or product from the folders the folder model gives that stage (`LA-EXP-DS03`), empty ones that can start a branch counted, so the nav, the graph's tree, the stage's page, the domain and product pages, counts, keyboard walking and search all follow. The skipped folder MUST have no row, group or address of its own; whatever would link to it links to the stage. A stage whose one folder is empty shows as a stage with no records.

title: One breadcrumb, collapsed past three places
statement: Every trail of places above a page (the header strip's, the wiki card's, the phone's top bar's, and any other) MUST be the one `Breadcrumb` component (`app/src/components/Breadcrumb.tsx`). A trail of up to three places MUST show in full; a longer one MUST show its first place (the product), a "…" button and its last place (the immediate parent). The button MUST be labeled with how many levels it hides and open a menu of the hidden levels, each a link, reached by Tab and the arrow keys and closed by Escape (focus back on the button) or a click elsewhere. Each place is one line cut with an ellipsis, its whole name in its tooltip.

title: Every stage works on every focus
statement: Every stage MUST draw something useful for every focus, so the stage switch is never disabled, dimmed or hidden and a stage chosen stays chosen as the focus moves:
notes:
- **Graph:** the focus in the one map, as `LA-V93` says.
- **ERD:** the product's one map (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19`), framed on the focus: a domain's region, an aggregate's boundary, an entity picked out in its aggregate; on any other record its nearest entity or aggregate above it, picked out in its domain (a table its entity), or its domain's region; for a Shared record (one in no domain) or a product, the whole map.
- **Trace:** the product's one All-at-once view (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19`, `LA-V98`): a record it draws (an outcome, a use case, an obligation, a record building one, a test) stands on its box, its whole path lit and the rest faded; any other record (a design record, an entity, a value object, a term, a group) shows the product's overview, the table under it showing the rows of the obligations whose chains hold it, or the explicit untraced state ("Nothing traces to this record: it serves no requirement or rule."), or the matrix around it.

The ERD's camera and fade are worked out by `erdFocus` (`app/src/erd/erd.ts`), the Trace's table by `traceShape` (`app/src/trace/chain.ts`) and its camera by the focus's box in its graph (`allGraph`, `app/src/trace/all.ts`); no code gates a stage by the focus's kind.

title: Panels never crowd the page: they collapse in set order before anything gets unreadably narrow
statement: Every floating panel MUST keep a readable width, and the stage's open space at least 300 px between its gaps: the wiki card shrinks to 360 px and no further, and the nav keeps the width it was given. When the window can't hold every open panel at that width, panels MUST collapse for space in a set order, the wiki card first, then the nav to its rail, and reopen in reverse order as the window widens; the chat, the Reader's task at hand, and a tool over the stage never collapse for space. A collapse for space MUST NOT change the Reader's own open or closed choice, and MUST show: the collapsed panel's toggle wears a dashed ring, and its tooltip and name say it is collapsed to give the stage room. Opening such a panel holds it open, the next panel in the order giving way instead, until it would fit anyway or the Reader closes it. Titles MUST wrap on whole words, a word breaking only when it is longer than the line (`overflow-wrap: break-word`, as for an ID), and no text MAY use `word-break: break-all`. A table too wide for its box MUST NOT be cut or scroll sideways: below 64rem of its container each row MUST stack (`.table-stack`), its header line first, then each of its cells at full width, wrapping, under its column's name, then its links; at 64rem and wider it stays a table.
notes: The rule is one function, `crowded` in `app/src/views/openSpace.ts`, from the window's width and the panels' widths: the shell (`App.tsx`) works it out, and the focus page reports its wiki card and any tool over the stage to it. The shell sets `--card-min` and `--stage-min` from the same numbers, so the card's CSS limits agree. With the chat open and every panel at its default width, the wiki card gives way first as the window narrows, then the nav; the widths at which each gives way are held by the rule's unit test, not here, so they change in one place.

title: Every stage is one map: focusing moves the camera, nothing re-lays out
statement: Every canvas stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) MUST lay a product out as one map, off the main thread, and again only when what the map reads changes (its tree, its labels or the text measure), never on a reload that left it alone, the map before it staying on screen and answering the camera until the new one is ready; every box MUST keep its place and size whatever is focused or filtered and however deep the depth shows. Focusing a record MUST move only the camera, gliding on the shared motion to frame it (at once on a stage switch, which keeps the focus, and under reduced motion). On the Graph's Tree a focus whose children's titles its frame would draw under 11 pixels MUST be framed by their column at reading size, the focus kept in view at the left edge, by one rule (`LA-EXP-DS09`). A filter, the depth or a focus that shows only part of the map MUST fade the rest back to the focus fade's strength, never take it out or lay the map out again. Each frame MUST draw only what is in view.
notes: One code does it for every stage: `useLaidOut` (`app/src/graph/layout.ts`) lays a map out in the layout's worker (`layout.worker.ts`), keyed by its packed input (`layout-input.ts`), and keeps the map shown until the new one arrives; the ERD keys ELK's layout by what it reads (`app/src/erd/layout.ts`); `keptFade` and `faintest` (`app/src/graph/fade.ts`) fade by place, a placed box's key, so a record a map draws twice can fade in one place and not the other; `frameRect` (`app/src/graph/camera.ts`) frames a rectangle of a map, and the graph's `frameOnMap` its tree, framing a focus's children's column when they would draw under `CHILD_READ_PX`; `useCameraGestures` (`app/src/graph/gestures.ts`) glides. The Graph's map is laid out by `placeTree` and `placeNested` (`app/src/graph/map.ts`, `nested.ts`, LA-V93-R16), the Trace stage's All-at-once view (`layOutColumns`, `app/src/trace/all-layout.ts`, LA-V98-R12) in its own worker (`useAllLaidOut`, `all-laid.ts`), keyed by what it reads, framed by `frameRect`.

title: Nothing replaces the stage: tools open as panels over it
statement: The stage MUST be what the Reader navigates, and no screen MAY replace it: every other screen is a tool over it. A tool (Checks, Appearance, the theme editor) MUST open as a frosted panel floating over the stage, which the open space leaves room for, and that never collapses for space (the other panels give way); a format page MUST open in the wiki card, the whole page; the products picker MUST be a card centered over the dimmed stage of the last product the Reader was in, or over an empty map on a first launch. Each MUST be layered on the current focus in the address's query (`?panel=checks`, `?panel=changes`, `?panel=appearance`, `?panel=theme&theme=<id>`, `?page=format/kinds/<kind>`), so the stage underneath keeps its place and every overlay is still a link; a move to another focus MUST keep the open tool open. Escape MUST close the topmost overlay, the one opened last, and focus MUST go back where it was before it opened. On a phone each MUST be a sheet.
notes: One module holds the addresses: `app/src/views/overlays.ts` reads them (`overlaysOf`), makes the links that open and close them (`panelHref`, `pageHref`, as patches of the current address that `app/src/router.tsx` applies), carries an open tool to a new focus (`carryOverlays`), closes the topmost on Escape (`useEscapeClosesTopmost`) and takes and gives back focus for every overlay, the dialogs included (`useOverlayFocus`). Every tool panel is `ToolPanelFrame` (`app/src/views/ToolPanel.tsx`), which floats at the left of the open space (`data-floating="left"`) and is a bottom sheet on a phone; the shell (`App.tsx`) counts its width in the crowding rule (LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18) as it does the chat's. The old full-screen addresses (`/<product-id>/checks`, `/format…`, `/settings/appearance`) are no pages.

title: Every stage has the same controls in the same places, every node reachable by keyboard
statement: Every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) MUST take its controls from one component each, so no stage can drift: a toolbar floating at the top of the open space, centered on the whole stage while it fits there (LA-V96-R05), holding first the shared controls in a fixed order (the step buttons Left, Right, Up and Down, each showing its arrow and its letter; Out and In between the levels; Frame, which frames the focus again), then the Changes controls (LA-V96-R28), then the stage's own controls; at the frame's bottom left corner the camera's zoom in, zoom out and fit the whole map, the same buttons, look and tooltips on every stage, never a canvas library's own; and along the bottom of the open space, on the camera's row, the stage's key bar (LA-V96-R30). When the toolbar does not fit its room it MUST give way in one fixed order: the names beside the icons and the baseline picker first, then the Changes controls fold into a More menu at its end, then the stage's secondary controls (the Graph's depth), then the step letters drop and the stage's own controls narrow. The walk's steps, Out, In, Frame and the stage's primary controls (the Graph's layouts and filters, the Trace's Gaps only) MUST stay in the row on every desktop width, down to 1024 px with the nav open, and fold into More only in the phone's form. A minimap and edge hints, where a stage has them, MUST sit in the same corner and style on every stage. Every stage MUST be a hierarchy the one stage walk moves over (`LA-V61-R49`), and from its product the walk's moves together MUST reach every node the stage draws.
notes:
- **The toolbar** (`StageToolbar`, `app/src/views/StageChrome.tsx`): its steps run the stage walk through the commands layer, as their keys do, so a button and its key never differ. It stays one row (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08`), stepping down through its tiers before paint (`TOOLBAR_FORMS`, which pins the fold order), measured against the room the open space gives it, so it widens again when the window grows or a panel collapses.
- **The camera** (`StageCamera`): zoom about the frame's middle, and fit the whole map in the frame; Frame in the toolbar (and `.`) frames the focus.
- **The levels** (`app/src/views/levels.ts`): each stage gives its hierarchy as parents, children in reading order, and its own move across siblings; Out, In and the going on at a container's edge are shared.
- **The key** (`StageKey`): one component for every stage's key bar, fed by each stage's own entries (`graphKeyEntries`, `erdKeyEntries`, `traceKeyEntries`) and the live marks every stage shares (`useChangesKey`); it measures its own rows before paint, wrapping to two and then scrolling sideways, and on a phone it is a Key chip that opens a sheet.

title: A change moves only what it changed
statement: When the data changes, every canvas stage (the Graph's Tree and Nested maps, the ERD and the Trace) MUST keep the map where the person left it. Adding, removing, renaming or moving a record under a parent MUST rearrange only that parent's region (for a move, the old and the new parent's): every other box keeps its exact place and size. Where a layout's rule makes a change spread (an equal split), the spread MUST stop at the changed parent, sized so its ancestors do not change. Existing siblings, rows and columns MUST keep their order: a new record is inserted at its place, and nothing is re-sorted on a change; an order a stage works out to shorten its lines is worked out again only on request (Tidy up in the toolbar), never on its own. What does move MUST glide from its old place to its new one on the shared motion, so the eye follows it (under reduced motion it lands at once, and the change stays as local). The camera MUST stay where it is on new data; when the focus's own box moved, the camera glides with it, keeping it where it was on screen.
notes: `app/src/graph/morph.ts` holds the morph (`useMorph`, `plateAt`) and the camera's follow (`followBox`), used by the Graph (`GraphPage.tsx`), the Trace's All-at-once view (`TraceAll.tsx`) and the ERD (`ErdView.tsx`, whose boxes glide by CSS in `styles.css`). The Tree and Nested layouts (`map.ts`, `nested.ts`) are top-down from each parent's fixed box, so a change under a parent re-lays only that parent's region; siblings' text and the Nested header band are fitted as if every sibling had children, and every label keeps the problem badge's room (`text.ts`), so nothing a child holds or shows sizes its siblings; the nav's tree orders records by kind, position and ID, never by title. The ERD (`app/src/erd/layout.ts`) is laid out bottom-up by ELK, so new data keeps each region's and the product's boxes where they were (`keepPlaces`): a grown box pushes only what it overlaps, a new one goes beside the rest, and its lines glide with the boxes (`app/src/erd/glide.ts`); Tidy up (`stageTidy`) lays the whole map out afresh. Deviation: the Graph's Map (`LA-EXP-DS12`, `app/src/graph/ground.ts`) sizes bottom-up, every leaf one size and each container as big as what it holds, so a change grows its containers and nudges what comes after each of them (the boxes after it in its area, the areas and neighborhoods after its own, the districts after its district), gliding; nothing before it moves and every container keeps its order. Deviation: the Trace's All-at-once view packs each column, so a record added or removed shifts the boxes below it in its column by a row (and what is placed beside them), gliding; every column keeps its order and nothing else is re-sorted.

title: Field inputs follow their column's type
statement: Each aggregate's editor MUST build its fields from the shared field inputs, one per column type: a line of text, long text, a whole number, yes or no, one of a column's values, a list, and a picker of the records a link may name; each input MUST take its label, whether it is required and its allowed values from its column in the schema.

title: A field input knows no kind
statement: A shared field input MUST NOT know a kind: it takes only its column and its value, and the aggregate's editor decides which inputs it shows and which command it sends.

title: A record's data file can be revealed, opened in the editor and its ID copied
statement: In the desktop app a record's facts MUST offer Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID for the data file that holds its row, and a right-click on a record row, a graph node or a record page's title MUST open a native menu of the same three. In a browser the app MUST show none of them.

title: Open in editor uses VS Code unless another editor is chosen
statement: Open in editor MUST open the record's data file in VS Code by default; File › Open Records In MUST offer Cursor, Zed, the system's default app and a command of the Owner's own from `settings.json`.

title: Every record ID shown is a link to that record
statement: Wherever a page shows a record ID, it MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to that record's page, so any reference can be followed or opened in a new tab.

title: A wiki page shows one level below its record by default
statement: A wiki page (product, domain, record or group) MUST show by default only the records one level below the page's own record. Anything deeper MUST be folded under its row and open only when the person opens it, opens everything, or searches for something inside it.

title: A folded row keeps its count and its marks
statement: A folded row MUST still show how many records it holds ("4 requirements") and its own coverage marks and problem badge, so nothing hidden is forgotten.

title: A record ID named in text is a link in the text, never a relation
statement: A record ID named in a text field MUST be shown only as a link in the text: it MUST NOT appear among the record's links out or in, in the graph, or in coverage.

title: Code and links in text are shown as written
statement: Turning named IDs into links MUST NOT change text inside code blocks, links the author wrote, or code spans holding anything besides one ID; a code span holding one lone record ID is wrapped in the link with its code style kept, and it MUST run only on the sanitized HTML.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link to it
statement: A list row that leads to one record MUST hold exactly one link that stands for the whole row, and that link MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to the record's page, so the row can be followed or opened in a new tab like any other reference. Other links in the row lead elsewhere and stay links of their own.

title: Links are shown by their labels, never by relation codes
statement: Wherever a page names a link, as a heading, a list title, a field label, an edge label or a tooltip, it MUST use the relation rule's `forward_label` read from the link's source or its `reverse_label` read from its target. A relation code such as `fulfills` or `hears` MUST NOT be shown as a heading or label; it may appear only as code, where a page explains how to write a link.

title: The record page shows the whole record, field by field
statement: The record page MUST show the record's ID, kind and title; its lead text (the one statement, goal, meaning or description its kind has), a test's When and Then as one scenario, and its notes, rendered as Markdown; its part rows laid out (an entity's or event's fields as a table, a flow's steps in order, a product's roles, a technical record's packages as one fact); its other columns as facts; and its parent and children.

title: The record page shows links both ways, grouped by relation
statement: The record page MUST show the record's outgoing links and its incoming links, each grouped by relation, with every linked record clickable.

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
statement: The HTML rendered from a record's text fields MUST be sanitized before it is put on the page, because records are written by agents as well as people.

title: The record page shows the problems about it
statement: The record page MUST list every problem whose record is this one.

title: Anywhere on a record's row opens that record
statement: In every list of records (the rows of a product, domain, record or group page, coverage gaps, open questions, what a requirement fulfills, the patterns a domain follows, and the problems on the checks page), a click anywhere on a row MUST open the record the row leads to, not only a click on its ID or title. Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click MUST open it in a new tab. The row's other controls (its fold chevron, other record links, badges and buttons) MUST keep doing what they do. Keyboard focus stays on the row's one link, and its focus ring and hover cover the whole row; a tree's arrow keys work as before.

title: Record IDs named in text are links
statement: In a record's rendered text fields (a record page, and a product's or domain's overview), every ID-shaped token that is the ID of a record of the space, other than the record itself, MUST become a link to the record's address, its bare ID (`/<id>`), with the record's title on hover, and a plain click MUST move within the app. An ID inside a code block, an existing link or a code span with other text MUST NOT be linked, nor part of a longer ID; a code span holding exactly one such ID MUST link.

title: An ID that names no record stays plain text
statement: An ID-shaped token in a text field that is no record of the space MUST be shown as written, as plain text: it MUST NOT be a link, and nothing reports it, since no check reads text for IDs.

title: Every list that can grow stays at ten rows, in every view
statement: Every list that can grow, including a wiki page's lists (its children, links and problems) and a group page's members, MUST use the long list: ten rows, then a scroll inside with a search box and a count.

title: Wiki pages open one level deep
statement: A product page MUST list its domains (and its summary and questions) but not their contents; a domain page its direct children grouped by kind (its five stages and open questions, each stage's kinds in the schema's order, and any other kind such as capabilities, in their `position`), each row showing its count of children; a record page its fields, its text, direct children and links; a group page its members. Each row with children MUST have a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, a chevron) and each section an Expand all / Collapse all button. What is opened MUST be remembered for the session while moving around. A search inside a section MUST reveal matching nested records by opening their row just for the match. Right arrow MUST open a row (or move into it) and Left close it (or move to its parent). The command palette MUST offer Expand all and Collapse all for the page.

title: Every list stays at 10 rows and can be searched
statement:
Every list in the spec pages (the menu's domains, a domain's record groups and nested lists, coverage gaps, problems and checks, open questions, a record's children and links both ways) MUST show up to 10 items as a plain list. With more than 10 it MUST show the first 10 rows' height and scroll inside, with a search box above it that filters by ID and title, a count such as "12 of 48", and a clear message when nothing matches.

The search box MUST be reachable with Tab, Escape MUST clear it, and the scrolling area MUST take focus so it scrolls from the keyboard. The list MUST know nothing about specs, so other views can use it.

title: Kinds and problem codes link to their format pages
statement: The wiki card's kind line MUST link to the kind's page, on a record page and on a group page. Every problem's code on the Checks panel, the domain page and the record page MUST link to its check's page.

title: Shell actions take only an ID
statement: The main process MUST accept an action from a page only on the action's own channel, as exactly `{ id }`, an ID in the record ID format, from a product window's own page. It MUST find what the action needs, such as the data file that holds the record's row, itself, and MUST NOT open, reveal or run anything a page names as a path.
